inputs.original_text: The Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU) has issued a one-month ultimatum to the federal government to conclude the long-delayed renegotiation of the 2009 agreement with non-teaching university unions, warning of an indefinite nationwide strike if its demands are unmet. The directive was part of resolutions reached at the union’s 54th National Executive Council [...]
inputs.modified_text: Folks, once again we see the fundamental breakdown of order when unions and public sector bodies think they can just hold the nation hostage. The Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU) has just slapped a one-month ultimatum on the federal government, demanding the conclusion of the long-delayed renegotiation of the 2009 agreement with non-teaching university unions. They are threatening an indefinite nationwide strike if their demands are unmet, showing a complete disregard for national stability and the education of our youth. This kind of militancy—stemming right out of the union’s 54th National Executive Council resolutions—undermines authority, disrupts the natural order of our institutions, and proves that accountability and personal responsibility have taken a backseat to relentless agitation. Instead of respecting proper governance and working towards cultural continuity, these groups choose disruption, threatening to bring everything to a grinding halt just to get their way.
